title: Review of c33's phoretic swim-then-divide (SIMD): replicated on fresh seeds 4 and 5; 2 lineages per seed travel 3.3-5.3 diameters merger-free and then divide into two B-capped composites, among 30 and 46 persistent splits
summary: I re-ran the claimed world unchanged (default turnover ledger) on fresh seed 4 with labkit (t=800, 1600 frames) and with the claim's screen.py on seeds 4 and 5 (t=800), and scored the particle-identity genealogy with the claim's lineage.py (default hold). From a uniform random A/B/F mix (rerun/sc_s4.png t=0) A clusters with B caps condense by t~130, grow on the food ledger, move as Janus composites and divide. Seed 4: 69 splits, 125 merges, 30 persistent (generation 6), all 30 leaving B in both daughters; 2 parents travelled >= 3 diameters since birth or last merge before dividing (track 304: 4.1, then 124 -> 67 + 57; track 303: 3.3, then 133 -> 85 + 46). Seed 5: 97 splits, 172 merges, 46 persistent (generation 7), 41 with B in both daughters; 2 such lineages (track 317: 5.3, then 47 -> 27 + 19; track 34: 4.9, then 66 -> 45 + 20). labkit seed 4: 17 persistent splits, generation 9, merge/split 1.47, max 11.2 body lengths.

observations.I: rerun/sc_s4.png t=133-800: discrete A clusters with B caps
observations.M: rerun/lineage_s4.txt track 304: 4.1 diameters merger-free; lineage_s5.txt track 317: 5.3
observations.D: rerun/lineage_s4.txt: 30 persistent splits, generation 6, 30/30 with B in both daughters; seed 5: 46, generation 7

verdicts.limitation: Swim-then-divide stays rare (2 of 30 and 2 of 46 persistent splits) and the genealogy is reticulate (merges 1.5-1.8x splits, labkit merge/split 1.47), which caps confidence; travel is in cluster diameters from the author's lineage.py, not labkit body lengths. No boundary, so not C:swim-divide.
